newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Fragile Estonian coalition beset by new problems.
newsitem.headline: Fragile Estonian coalition beset by new problems.

text.p: Estonia's fragile government looked even shakier on Friday when Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi's party signed a deal with the main opposition party.
Commentators described the cooperation pact between Vaehi's Coalition Party and the opposition Centre Party as a slap in the face for the Reform Party.
Although Coalition and Reform are still partners in government, the year-old alliance has looked threatened since they campaigned vigorously against each other in October's local elections.
"In this new situation it is difficult for the Reform Party to see itself continuing in government," Reform Party secretary general Heiki Kranich told Estonian radio.
But Vaehi, who heads Estonia's sixth government since it quit the former Soviet Union in 1991, said the deal with the Centre Party was not aimed at split the current coalition.
He said bringing the Centre Party into the government could help stabilise the political situation.
"At the moment we have agreed to coordinate how we are going to vote in parliament. The agreement is not aimed at destroying the current coalition," Vaehi told Reuters.
"We will start thinking about a new coalition after the old one no longer exists."
